question.text: In which decade will the 2026 UK Christmas number one have been originally released?
question.resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as the decade of the original release of the 2026 [UK Christmas number one](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones).
question.fine_print:
This question will resolve based on the release date of the specific recording that tops the charts. It is immaterial whether a different version of the single was recorded and released previously. 
For example in 2004, this question would have resolved as 2000s because that year's Christmas number one: Band Aid 20's version of "Do They Know It's Christmas?," was released in 2004, even though the original "Do They Know It's Christmas?" was recorded and released in 1984.
Each decade will be defined by the first three digits of the year. For example, any recording released between January 1, 1990, and December 31, 1999, will be considered a 1990s release.

research:
## 1. Resolution source

- 2026-11-01: The [Wikipedia list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones) runs up to 2025, with Kylie Minogue's "XMAS" as the latest entry. It has nothing on 2026 yet. The list follows the Official Charts Company (OCC) Official Singles Chart for Christmas week. Christmas Day 2026 is a Friday, so that chart should be published around 25 Dec. This fits the resolution date of about 26 Dec.
- 2025-12-19: The OCC named Kylie Minogue's "XMAS" (an Amazon Music Original, 2025 release) as the 2025 Christmas number 1. Wham!'s "Last Christmas" (1984) was No. 2, Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" (1994) was No. 3, and Together For Palestine's "Lullaby" was No. 5. [OCC](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2025-kylie-minogue-xmas/)
- I did not find a raw data file for the chart. The OCC weekly chart pages are the primary data.

## 2. Current status

- Nothing has settled the question yet. The Christmas chart is about 8 weeks away.
- 2026-10-30: Jamie Miller's "BABYDOLL" is at number 1 for a second week. It was his first UK number 1 on the 23 Oct chart. [OCC 23/10](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20261023/7501/), [OCC current](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/)
- 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-16: Taylor Swift's "Patient Zero" was number 1, its third week on top by 16 Oct. [OCC 16/10](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20261016/7501/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)

- 2026-11-01: Mariah Carey released her yearly "It's Time" video, which marks the start of Christmas streaming season. [Just Jared](https://www.justjared.com/2026/11/01/mariah-carey-goes-punk-before-declaring-its-time-for-christmas-watch-now/)
- 2026-11-01: Big UK retailers (Tesco, Argos, Sainsbury's and others) have launched their Christmas adverts. None of the coverage I saw mentions a song tie-in that could chart. [Metro](https://metro.co.uk/2026/11/01/biggest-2026-christmas-adverts-far-including-richard-ayoade-scrooge-29753308/)
- 2026-10-21: OLBG published "theoretical" odds. Bookmakers were not taking bets at the time. Wham! were 1/3, Sam Fender and Olivia Dean 6/4, Ella Langley 2/1, and Olivia Rodrigo, Taylor Swift and Ed Sheeran 3/1 each. Kylie was 4/1, Ashe 6/1, Sidemen 10/1 and Bov Boys 12/1. LadBaby, who were 8/1 on 12 Oct, were no longer listed. [OLBG 21 Oct](https://www.olbg.com/news/christmas-number-one-2026-odds-betting-experts-back-last-christmas-reclaim-christmas-number-one-spot)
- 2026-10-12: OLBG's earlier list had Wham! at 1/2. It said prices would move once release schedules and radio playlists are settled. [OLBG 12 Oct](https://www.olbg.com/news/christmas-number-one-2026-odds-wham-set-early-festive-pace)
- I found no confirmed charity single or Christmas number 1 bid announced for 2026. The LadBaby "withdrawal" articles I found seem to date from 2023, so they do not tell us about 2026. [Express & Star](https://www.expressandstar.com/whats-on/arts-and-entertainment/ladbaby-end-christmas-chart-dominance-as-pair-withdraw-from-festive-race-5837063)

**How the contenders map to the answer options:**
- **1980s:** Wham!'s "Last Christmas" (1984).
- **2020s:** every other named contender, including Kylie's "XMAS" (2025), Sam Fender and Olivia Dean's "Rein Me In" (2025), Ella Langley's "Choosin' Texas" (2025), Swift's "Patient Zero" (2026), and any new charity or YouTuber single.
- **1990s:** Mariah Carey's "All I Want for Christmas Is You" (1994). It has never been the UK Christmas number 1 and finished 3rd in 2024 and 2025.

## 4. Base rates

From the [Wikipedia list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones):
- **2010 to 2019:** all 2010s releases (X Factor winners, Military Wives, Justice Collective, NHS Choir, Clean Bandit, Ed Sheeran, LadBaby 2018 and 2019).
- **2020 to 2022:** all 2020s releases (LadBaby). "Food Aid" in 2022 was a new recording, so it counts as 2020s.
- **2023 and 2024:** 1980s, from Wham!'s "Last Christmas", originally released in 1984.
- **2025:** 2020s (Kylie's "XMAS").

So over the last 16 years the winner was a song released that same decade 14 times, and the 1980s won twice. Since LadBaby stopped competing in 2023, it has been 2 for the 1980s and 1 for the 2020s. Before 2023, the most recent Christmas number 1 from an earlier decade was a re-entry in 1991: Queen's "Bohemian Rhapsody / These Are the Days of Our Lives", a double A-side reissue. Whether that counts as a 1970s recording is a technicality.

## 5. Other forecasts

- 2026-10-21: OLBG's theoretical odds, as listed in section 3. The 1/3 price on Wham! implies about 75% before adjusting for the bookmaker's margin. Converting all the 2020s contenders together gives a large share, but the odds add up to well over 100% (a heavily over-round book), so they need normalising before use. [OLBG](https://www.olbg.com/news/christmas-number-one-2026-odds-betting-experts-back-last-christmas-reclaim-christmas-number-one-spot)
- The Punter's Page shows "Last Christmas" at 3/10, but this price may be left over from the 2025 market. [The Punter's Page](https://www.thepunterspage.com/christmas-number-one-odds/)
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets cover the UK Christmas number 1; they are about the US Billboard chart. Kalshi has "All I Want for Christmas Is You" at 74% to rank 1 or 2 on the Billboard Hot 100 dated 19 Dec 2026. That shows strong US holiday streaming, but it does not decide the UK result. "Choosin' Texas" is at 99% to be Hot 100 number 1 in November. That is a sign of its crossover strength, though it is a US chart.
- I could not find a Manifold, Metaculus or live Oddschecker market for 2026. The Oddschecker page shows the 2025 market. [Oddschecker](https://www.oddschecker.com/novelty/christmas-specials/christmas-number-one)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution

- Early to mid November: Christmas back-catalogue songs start to come back into the chart as streaming rises, and bookmakers will probably open real markets.
- Mid November to early December: big pop releases, such as possible deluxe or festive versions from Swift, Sheeran or Rodrigo, or a festive version of "Rein Me In". Kylie or Amazon could also push "XMAS" again or bring out a new exclusive.
- Late November to December: any charity or YouTuber single (Sidemen, Bov Boys, a LadBaby comeback, a campaign like Together For Palestine) would usually be released one to two weeks before Christmas.
- Around 18 to 24 Dec: the tracking week for the Christmas chart. Around 25 Dec: the OCC announces the Christmas number 1.

# 2026 UK Christmas number one: research summary

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the Wikipedia [List of UK singles chart Christmas number ones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_UK_singles_chart_Christmas_number_ones), which takes its result from the Official Charts Company. There is no data file. The 2026 entry will be added after the announcement. I did not fetch the Wikipedia page itself.
- 2025-12-19: The 2025 winner was Kylie Minogue's "XMAS", an Amazon Music Original from 2025, so a 2020s release. The rest of the 2025 Christmas chart: "Last Christmas" (Wham!, 1984) at 2, "All I Want for Christmas Is You" (Mariah Carey, 1994) at 3, "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree" (Brenda Lee, 1958) at 4, "Lullaby" (Together For Palestine) at 5, "Fairytale of New York" (1987) at 6, "Raindance" (Dave and Tems) at 7 and "Underneath the Tree" (Kelly Clarkson, 2013) at 8. [Official Charts](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/christmas-number-1-2025-kylie-minogue-xmas/)
- 2026-10-26: Official Charts says the 2026 race runs from Friday 18 December to Christmas Eve at 11:59pm. The winner is expected on Christmas Day, Friday 25 December, on BBC Radio 1. This will be the 75th Christmas number one. [Official Charts](https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/when-will-the-christmas-number-1-2026-be-announced/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has been settled yet. Counting for the chart that decides the question starts on 18 December 2026.

The rest of the top 5 is "Housewife", "Stop the Wedding", "Expectations" and "Great Expectation". Taylor Swift's "Patient Zero" was number 1 on the 16 October chart. [Official Charts](https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/)

## 4. Base rates
These recent winners and release dates are from my own knowledge, not checked against the Wikipedia page during this research:
- 2014: Ben Haenow, 2014 release (2010s)
- 2015 to 2017: NHS Choir, then Clean Bandit "Rockabye", then Ed Sheeran "Perfect", all released in the same year they won (2010s)
- 2018 to 2019: LadBaby, 2010s
- 2020 to 2022: LadBaby, 2020s
- 2023 and 2024: Wham! "Last Christmas" (1984), 1980s
- 2025: Kylie Minogue "XMAS", 2020s

What this shows:
- In the last 12 years, 10 winners were released in the same year they won. The other 2 were the 1980s Wham! wins.
- The last 1990s winner was 2009: Rage Against the Machine, "Killing in the Name", a 1992 recording.
- Mariah Carey has never been UK Christmas number one.
- Christmas falling on a Friday matches 2020, a LadBaby year, so there is no special pattern to read into the calendar.
- In practice the race is between the 1980s ("Last Christmas", possibly "Fairytale of New York") and the 2020s (any new or 2025-26 release, such as "XMAS", "Rein Me In" or a charity single). Smaller tails are the 1990s (Mariah, 1994) and 1950s/"1960s or earlier" (Brenda Lee, 1958).

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on the UK Christmas number one.
- The Kalshi markets that were provided are about the US Billboard Hot 100, not the UK chart, but they show how strong Mariah's song still is:

  - The prices listed for the 26 December chart show mostly low ranks for it.

- The listed Oddschecker market page ([link](https://www.oddschecker.com/novelty/christmas-specials/christmas-number-one)) showed 2025 prices. I could not find a live 2026 page.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Christmas adverts (Tesco, Argos and others) and the Mariah video launched around 1 November, so Christmas streaming will now build.
- 1980s and 1990s classics usually peak in mid to late December.
- A new Christmas single or re-release from Kylie, Ed Sheeran, Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo, the Sidemen or LadBaby, or a charity single, could be announced in November or December. I found no confirmation of any of these.
- Kylie won in 2025 with Amazon Music promotion plus CD and vinyl sales. Watch for a similar physical-sales push in 2026.
- Weekly UK charts on 4, 11 and 18 December show who is leading before the race.
- The race runs from 18 to 24 December, and the result is announced on 25 December 2026.

(a) **Time left:** about 8 weeks. The Christmas chart covers roughly 18 to 24 December 2026 and should be announced around 25 December.

(b) **Status quo:** No Christmas-week chart exists yet. The default Christmas pattern is Wham!'s "Last Christmas" (1984) climbing to number 1 as streaming builds, as it did in 2023 and 2024. The current number 1, Jamie Miller's "BABYDOLL", is a 2020s release, but it will almost certainly not hold through Christmas.

(c) **Base rates:**
- **Last 16 years:** 14 winners were released in the same decade they won, and 2 were from the 1980s (Wham! in 2023 and 2024).
- **Since LadBaby stopped competing (2023 to 2025):** 1980s twice, 2020s once (Kylie's "XMAS", which won through an Amazon exclusive and a strong sales push).
- **1990s:** Mariah Carey has never been the UK Christmas number 1 and finished 3rd in both 2024 and 2025.
- **Other older songs:** classics from the 1950s to 1970s (Slade, Wizzard, Brenda Lee) hardly ever reach number 1.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **21 Oct 2026, OLBG theoretical odds:** Wham! 1/3. Sam Fender and Olivia Dean 6/4, Ella Langley 2/1, Swift, Rodrigo and Sheeran 3/1 each, Kylie 4/1. These are not live markets and the book is heavily over-round. After normalising, Wham! comes out around 45 to 55%.
- **19 Dec 2025:** Kylie beat Wham! (No. 2) and Mariah (No. 3). This shows a coordinated 2020s push can still win.
- **Charity and YouTuber bids:** no 2026 charity or YouTuber bid has been confirmed so far. LadBaby is out of the running.
- **Live markets:** no liquid market covers this exact question. The Kalshi markets are about the US Billboard chart.

(e) **Unexpected-outcome scenario:** Mariah Carey's streams surge and she edges out Wham! for the first time, giving a 1990s result. Alternatively, a viral TikTok revival of an older track wins, such as an early-2010s song or a 1950s to 1970s classic.

**How I moved from the base rate:** I started near 60% for the 1980s, based on Wham! winning two of the last three years and its bookmaker favouritism. I moved down to about 52% because Kylie's 2025 win shows the 2020s path is real. That path includes a strong pop release, a festive tie-in, or a late charity or YouTuber single, all of which usually appear only in December. I kept small amounts on the 1990s (Mariah) and on the remaining tail options.
